thread:
alex: FYI CI artifacts spiked after the new attention-kernel merge, noticed +11.8MB per linux-x86 fatbin.
maya: ouch. where is the bloat coming from? fatbin, PTX or extra object sections?
alex: looks like we started embedding PTX for more archs and left debug sections. cuobjdump shows multiple PTX blobs for sm_70 sm_75 sm_80 sm_86 sm_90.
jin: shipping PTX for every SM is intended for forward compat, but we don't need full list for Dedicated builds. Can we filter the gencode list at package time?
sam: we filter at build-time sometimes but it's brittle. If we drop PTX for older SMs we lose forward compatibility on some customers' older AWS instances.
maya: idea: produce two artifacts: "compat" (with broad PTX) and "min" (only target arches we test). CI publishes both and runtime picks the smaller when allowed.
alex: that would double CI artifacts though, and increases publish cost.
buildbot: [build #4821] linux-x86 fatbin size: 24.3MB -> new merge increased to 36.1MB. Attached: build.log
jin: another approach: LTO + strip debug sections + compress the fatbin. LTO tends to collapse duplicate kernels across SM variants.
maya: agree. NVCC flags we used earlier were basic. Proposed nvcc flags snippet:

```
nvcc -O3 -lineinfo \ 
  -gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 \ 
  -gencode=arch=compute_86,code=sm_86 \ 
  -Xcompiler "-fdata-sections -ffunction-sections" \ 
  -Wl,--gc-sections \ 
  -Xlinker -s  # final strip
```

alex: try also `-Xlinker --icf=all`? (link-time identical code folding) But I think that's for host linker only.
jin: ptxas and nvcc have options for reducing PTX verbosity: `--compress-all`? I haven't used that. We could post-process with `cuobjdump` + `objcopy --remove-section` to strip sections we don't need.
sam: objcopy on ELF helps, but fatbin sections are embedded. We could run zstd on the fatbin payload in CI and have runtime transparently decompress — adds startup cost though.
maya: we discussed runtime micropatching before: ship a tiny kernel selector stub and fetch additional PTX on demand from CDN when runtime detects an unsupported SM. That avoids shipping all PTX by default.
alex: micropatching is neat but adds runtime network dependency and complexity for air-gapped Private deployments.
jin: can be hybrid: default to local min artifact, and for hosted we allow fetch; private tenants get compat artifact.
sam: CI gating: set size threshold for min-artifact (e.g., < 28MB) and fail if over. compat artifact can be exempt but must report.
maya: propose changes to CI config:

```
- add job: build:min-artifact (arch-filtered, lto, strip)
- add job: build:compat-artifact (broad-ptx, lto optional)
- size-gate: fail on build:min-artifact if > 30MB
- publish both to S3 with metadata tag: artifact-type
```

alex: who picks the arch list for min? we should derive from the build matrix of supported pool GPUs and recent telemetry (last 90d).
jin: I'll add a script that generates `arch-list.txt` from supported.json and telemetry. script idea:

```
python tools/gen_arch_list.py --last-90-days --threshold 0.5 > arch-list.txt
nvcc --gencode-from-file arch-list.txt
```

sam: also add CI job to run `cuobjdump --fatbin -s` and compute per-section sizes, post as artifact so reviewers can quickly see which section grew.
maya: good. Also add regression alert in PR check if fatbin increased >5% vs base branch.
alex: permissions: we must ensure Dedicated runtime still has fallback to a compatible kernel if users have older hardware.
jin: runtime fallback map exists; we can wire it to prefer locally available kernels then remote-fetch.
buildbot: NOTE: previous micropatch prototype added 120ms cold-start when fetching extra ptx for first use. Needs async fetch and cache.
sam: action items:
- jin: implement gen_arch_list.py and arch-filtered build (owner)
- maya: update CI pipeline config and size gate (owner)
- alex: design runtime fetch fallback doc and compatibility policy (owner)
- sam: add cuobjdump size artifact and PR regression check (owner)

alex: cool, let's try a small experiment on a branch and run one matrix build.
maya: I'll kick it off after lunch and post results here :thumbsup:
alex: thanks.@maya
maya: np :rocket:
